_note: AGES 16-17 (session P2b, GDD 4.10 decision 6 'P2b's questions'; format in README.md): the driving school, a summer job, a teammate really quitting or joining (the effect `team`: the group, its level and its pull change for real), the upper-secondary school's people (a lukio group supervisor and counsellor, classmates, a vocational workshop) and the social life of 16-17. Real-world facts only as far as data/romance.json research reads them: the car licence at 18 (no practice rules stated), a person of 15 can sign a work contract, no night work under 18. The driving school and the summer job are story beats (a real choice that takes slots of the coming week); the school's people and friends are feed messages and invitations; everything is guarded by age / stage / flag conditions so it never contradicts the player.

text: Half of your friends have signed up for driving school before they turn 18. The theory course is two evenings a week. Should we put your name down this week, or wait until the training allows?
The driving school sent the autumn course dates. You would be on the road with your own licence at 18 if you start now. It takes two evenings this week.

replies.label: Start the theory course
replies.hint: Tuesday and Thursday evenings are the course
replies.result: Put down. You will be driving us to the lake by next year.

replies.label: Not now
replies.result: Fine. The licence will wait; the track will not.

text: The driving school called. Your next lesson is on the calendar next to your training plan. I will drive you there.
I found the driving school's bill in the post. Worth every cent, as long as you also learn to park.
Dad asked who is nervous about your driving lessons. The answer was Dad.
I passed the theory exam today. Seventeen out of twenty. Next the lessons, then I drive us to the lake. You are coming.
Everyone is talking about driving school. I am scared of the driving part. Parallel parking is witchcraft.
The sports shop in town needs a hand for a week: weekdays, daytime only, since you are under 18. It pays real money. Your training stays the same; the evenings would be for resting.
A neighbour runs a garden centre and needs help for a week. Weekday days, home by five. Do you want it? It would be your own money.

replies.label: Take the week
replies.hint: weekday evenings are early nights after work
replies.result: I will ring them. Your first own money!

replies.label: Not this time
replies.result: Okay. There is always next year.

text: Your pay arrived. Own money feels different, doesn't it. Dad says save half. Mum says buy new spikes.
I saw your pay come in. Proud of you. Working and training in the same week is not nothing.
The owner rang to say you worked well and that you are welcome back next year.
The shop said you were on time every day and never complained. That is the best reference there is.
I am stopping athletics at the end of this week. School and the band take all my time, and I would rather do two things well. I wanted you to hear it from me.
I have decided to quit the group. My knee never really got better and I miss my weekends. It was fun running with you.
A new runner joined the group this week. Show them the warm-up route and be kind: everyone remembers their first week.
We have a new runner in the group from this week. They are nervous. You were once too.
Welcome to lukio. I am your group supervisor. Here you plan your own courses with the study counsellor, so the timetable is yours; my door is open.
First weeks in lukio are always a bit chaotic. Everyone is new to everyone. If something is unclear, come and find me.
A timetable for an athlete is a puzzle, and I like puzzles. My door is open if your courses and your training start to fight.
Many of my students train twice a day and still pass everything. It takes planning, not luck.
We have to hand in a group work for the biology course. Can we do it at mine on {weekday}? It is easier than doing it on the bus.
Group work on {weekday} at the library: three people, one project, one sad PowerPoint. Join us?

replies.label: Yes, I will be there
replies.hint: your study evening, with {from}; grades ▲ a little
replies.result: You divided the slides fairly and finished before nine.

replies.label: I will do my part alone
replies.result: Okay. Send me your slides by Thursday.

text: Everyone is stressing about their courses. Sit next to me tomorrow, I will share my notes. You have enough on your plate.
I wrote a summary of the whole period for the course you missed. It is on the shared drive. You are welcome.
Our workshop teacher said our class is the first to finish the project on time. Next we do one for a real customer. It smells like sawdust and success.
My hands are black from the workshop and I have never been so tired of something so good. See you tomorrow.
We got tickets for the festival on {weekday}. The whole afternoon and the evening, five bands, one muddy field. Come with us.
A festival day on {weekday}. We will take the early bus and be back whenever. You have to come.

replies.label: I am in
replies.result: Three bands, one lost shoe, and a very late bus home.

replies.label: I will come for the afternoon
replies.result: The afternoon bands were the better ones anyway.

text: Someone's parents are lending us their cabin on {weekday}. Sauna, a fire, cards and no one to say bedtime. Come.
Cabin on {weekday}. Eight of us, one fireplace, a big pot of pasta. Say you are coming.

replies.label: I am in
replies.result: You talked by the fire until the sky went light.

replies.label: I will come, but go to bed early
replies.result: You were the first to sleep and the first to wake up.

replies.label: Not this weekend
replies.result: We will take lots of photos for you.

text: You have been sensible about your evenings lately, and we have noticed. You have the house key from now on, and we trust you with it.
We have been thinking: you are older now, and you handle both school and training. We will ask less. We still worry a little, it is our job.
